attacks.claim: go.mod adds `replace go.uber.org/zap => ../zap`, a local filesystem path. CI builds from a clean checkout where ../zap does not exist, so the build fails, or it picks up an unreviewed local fork. The release binary is not reproducible or buildable from main.

The dry-run printPlan does not match the real computeBatches. It uses floor (int(...)) instead of ceil, so batch sizes differ. It also computes the batch size over all hosts instead of the hosts left after removing the canary. And it does not remove the canary from the host list, so the canary appears twice, in batch 0 and again in a later batch. The plan on-call is told to trust is therefore wrong. For example, with 10 hosts and surge 0.25, dry-run uses 2 per batch while the real run uses 3.
attacks.evidence: per := int(float64(len(hosts)) * o.MaxSurge) ... for i := 0; i < len(hosts); i += per  vs  computeBatches: math.Ceil(float64(len(rest)) * o.MaxSurge) with rest = without(hosts, o.CanaryHost)

attacks.claim: The batching logic is duplicated in printPlan instead of reusing computeBatches. That duplication caused the divergence above and will keep drifting. printPlan should render the output of computeBatches.
attacks.evidence: func printPlan(...) re-implements batching; computeBatches is unchanged and unused in the dry-run path

attacks.claim: The zap dependency moves to an unreleased pseudo-version, and the replace directive points at an unreviewed local directory. This is an unvetted supply-chain change bundled into a feature PR. The pseudo-version also does not match the replace target, so what actually gets built is unclear.
No tests are included for the dry-run path or for parity between the plan and the real batches. The PR description claims the plan is exactly what will run, but nothing verifies it.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: tests for printPlan / dry-run parity with computeBatches
